llm.summary: This image-generation skill is coherent and disclosed, but users should be deliberate because it sends prompts and selected files to a third-party paid service and stores an API key locally.

dimensions.detail: Network use, prompt transmission, selected local-file uploads, hosted output URLs, and possible paid API usage are disclosed and proportionate to cloud image generation.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The install path is a pinned npm CLI package with an npx alternative; this is disclosed, though it relies on a third-party package rather than bundled code.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The trigger phrases include generic image-generation wording, which could invoke this third-party service for ordinary image requests unless the user is explicit.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill discloses local API-key persistence in ~/.dlazy/config.json and supports environment-variable use and revocation; external package inspection showed ordinary config-file writing, so users on shared systems should verify file permissions.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The skill's stated purpose is Nano Banana 2.0 text-to-image and image-to-image generation, and the documented dlazy banana2 CLI flow matches that purpose.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install this only if you are comfortable using dLazy as the image-generation provider. Treat prompts and any reference images or local paths you pass as data sent to dLazy, expect API-key storage unless you use DLAZY_API_KEY per invocation, and use dry-run or explicit confirmation before billable calls when cost matters.
llm.findings: [SQP-1] expected: The English and Chinese generic trigger terms fit an image-generation skill, but they do increase accidental invocation risk for a paid third-party API; this is a user-control note rather than evidence of hidden or malicious behavior.
